invariants.rule: Closing a lead records a structured reason and optional note, Other requires an explanation, closed reasons remain searchable, and a new customer reply reopens the conversation and clears the closure details.
Buyer-alert onboarding assumes Buying when intent is unstated, persists that default, proceeds directly to sale budget bands, and offers Renting instead as an explicit exception.

Buyer locations accept Bengaluru real-estate market zones (CBD & Off-CBD, SBD, ORR and PBD East/South/North) plus directional zones, normalize Bangalore and Bengaluru spellings, and match inventory in member localities without leaking into unrelated zones.

A buyer's stated locality matches inventory across spelling variants, listings in that locality lead every buyer-facing shortlist ordered by property-type fit before nearby listings, and a stated plot type matches plot listings rather than houses.

A single stated plot size admits larger plots up to 35% over as near-fits ranked below exact fits and within-10% near-misses, including when a full brief clamps their scores; smaller plots and plots beyond that headroom are excluded, and a stated size band keeps its strict cap.

A lead asking for more listings receives the next matches the share ledger says they have not seen, with nothing filed and no question asked; the qualification ladder never asks a rung twice in a thread; relative size feedback never stores a floor above the cap it cleared.

The latest outbound sender owns qualification replies: a later agent message keeps the bot quiet, while a later bot message resumes automation so an older agent message cannot leave a fresh buyer requirement unanswered.

A Meta error that blocks Marketing to one recipient — the frequency cap 131049 and the experiment block 130472 — never changes the composed message body: it records structured failure metadata under Meta's own code, pauses only Marketing templates for that contact (at least 24 hours for the cap, a 30-day horizon for the experiment), defers queued alerts without consuming retries, clears the pause when the contact replies, and gives web and mobile agents a friendly status naming the cause with no immediate resend action; Utility templates remain eligible. Only a verdict from Meta sets a pause: the dispatcher and the status webhook each keep whichever standing pause runs longer, and a send the local guard itself refused never extends one, so retries cannot hold a pause open indefinitely.

A lead who taps "Close my enquiry" on a check-in or enquiry template is asked, after the acknowledgement, why the shared property did not fit: the property is resolved from the quoted template, the last week of outbound messages or the recorded enquiry; the one-tap reason (budget, location, type, size, bought elsewhere, not buying now, other) is filed on listing feedback, the contact timeline and the active journey item, the agent is notified, both messages bypass the dead-contact gate, and the question never promises to be the last message.

"Close my enquiry" closes the enquiry on the listing the template named, not the lead: that listing is rejected for the contact and its journey branch dropped, the contact stays live, matching and on whatever alert consent they last gave, and the acknowledgement says their other enquiries stay open. After the drop-off reason (or at once when the close names no listing) the lead is shown their open enquiries (active journey branches not already at a closing or won stage) as a one-tap list — close any of them, or keep them all, each answer logged on the journey — and then the requirement ladder or their current matches; "bought elsewhere" and "not buying right now" instead park the search by marking the contact dead, and the drop-off reason is filed on the branch the close already dropped. Only a close that names no listing on a journey with nothing open marks the contact dead, and START ALERTS in the lead's own words revives a dead contact, un-parks the requirement and grants consent before the confirmation and ladder go out.

A funnel keyword buried in a lead’s text question never restarts a flow that lead has already been through: once a listing has been sent to them, or they ask for a person, the matched flow is skipped and the question is answered from that listing instead. Asking for a person counts whether typed or tapped: a template quick reply whose label asks for a person ("Talk to someone", "Call me back") gets the same callback promise, agent notification, bridged relay and pending flag as a typed "call me". Any other quick-reply label is never read as a question. A tap is matched against flow keywords by its raw label, never the inbox's decorated rendering, so an exact-match flow keyed on a label opens on that tap. A flow they have never entered still opens on its own keyword, and a lead who has been sent nothing is still qualified by the funnel. Entry only — an active run still advances.

tests.case: [INB-011] reads a quick-reply tap asking for a person as a callback request
does not restart a flow on a quick-reply tap that asks for a person
opens an exact-match flow keyed on the tapped label

invariants.rule: The shipped showcase funnel enters on openers and explicit intent phrases only, never on a bare word a property conversation is made of. The flow builder warns, without blocking activation, when a contains-matched entry keyword is such a word, and no shipped template trips that warning. A showcase flow still carrying a stock keyword list is moved to the tightened one; an edited list is left alone.

An inbox attachment is staged straight into the account's own chat-media prefix under a server-signed, single-path upload URL rather than through the app, so the caps the composer advertises (5 MB image, 16 MB video, 100 MB document) are the caps that apply; web and mobile refuse an unsupported type or an oversized file in the same words before uploading, and a media send reads the staged object back and refuses one that is missing, outside the account, or larger than Meta's cap before handing the link to Meta.

The qualification ladder never drops or re-asks what a lead already said: a bare size ("1200 sqft", "30x40") is filed as a requirement, lines of one burst are filed together and in order whatever order their webhooks land in, one conversation is qualified by one webhook at a time under the inbound chain's conversation lease (INB-016), never a second lease of its own (same-second lines are ordered by their ingestion sequence), buy-or-rent follows the newest line of the burst that states it (a bare "Rent" correcting "Buy" included) so no older webhook undoes a newer one, and a budget no rent could reach (₹10 L+, ₹1 Cr+ for commercial) answers buy-or-rent. A lead who asks for matches when nothing fits is told what was searched and asked the next missing rung, never told to change a brief they never gave.

When nothing fits a lead's brief but their own locality has live listings of the same deal type at another price or type, the no-match reply (the requirement playback card and the on-demand matches reply) names how many, their price band (monthly rent for rentals, as the matching engine prices them; one deal type per band, with untyped listings read as Sale) and, only when the lead's budget is on the same basis, whether it is above or below it, with a link scoped to those listings; when there are more than the link carries, the reply says the link shows the ones closest to the budget (or the most affordable) and a scan that hits its bound is stated as "N+". Housing-board prefixes such as "KHB" never stop a locality from matching.

Every automated handler for an inbound WhatsApp message (control replies, the owner chatbot, update sessions, qualification, flows, lead Q&A and automations) runs for one conversation one message at a time under a single conversation lease taken after the message is stored, so overlapping webhooks never start two flow runs, advance a flow step twice, or double-send a condition-guarded automation, and only the earliest of racing first messages fires first_inbound_message. A run that waited reads the contact and conversation afresh. A webhook that cannot get the lease in time hands the holder its whole handler context (never the access token), and the holder reruns the full chain for it exactly once; a deferred id with no stored context is only qualified, and a live lease that cannot take the message logs and skips the handlers rather than running them unlocked. A claim that still errors after three short retries (about two seconds), or a missing service-role client, is treated as that same busy case: nothing runs unlocked. A holder never deletes a lease that may carry deferred ids: when it hits its deferred-rounds cap or its finish fails it lets the lease expire, and the next holder of the conversation runs what was left after its own message and clears each payload as it takes it. Different conversations run in parallel.

A cron resume of a waiting automation runs exactly once and never inside an inbound chain: each due automation_pending_executions row is claimed atomically under a claim token before it runs (overlapping cron runs split the rows, never share one), and only that claim settles it as done or failed. The resume runs under the same conversation lease as INB-016 (the row's conversation, else the contact's thread), never waits for it: a live lease, or a lease claim that stays indeterminate, releases the claim and leaves the row pending for the next tick without spending an attempt. The resume holds the lease for at most about 20 seconds, shorter than an inbound waiter's 30, so an inbound message is not deferred to it, and it never runs deferred inbound ids: it lets the lease expire with them for the next inbound holder. A row stuck running past 15 minutes is reclaimed, and after 3 attempts it is marked failed. Immediately before it executes, a resume re-asserts its claim token (refreshing claimed_at) and skips a row another run has reclaimed. A failed conversation lookup releases the claim rather than running unlocked; only a contact with no conversation, or no contact, runs unlocked, since there is nothing to serialise against. A batch runs up to five conversations at once, each conversation's rows one at a time in run_at order, so a slow resume never holds up another conversation; automation webhooks time out after 10 seconds, and rows not started within the route's time budget are released back to pending.

Agents can merge any two confirmed duplicate contacts from web or mobile, explicitly choose the surviving record, retain every distinct phone number and complementary profile or requirement data, and consolidate both one-to-one Inbox histories before hiding the duplicate.

From a contact's record on web or mobile, agents can share the account's property portal link from the business WhatsApp number or their personal WhatsApp; the link opens on the contact's recorded interests with Pulse attribution, the message tells a buyer to filter, shortlist and send the enquiry from the portal, an Agent-classified contact instead gets the link in agent view (mode=view) with co-broker copy about forwarding listings with their own share link, a closed 24-hour window falls back to the approved property selection template, and a personal share is noted on the contact's timeline.

From a buyer contact's record on web or mobile, agents can hand-pick up to 25 listings and send them through the showcase share flow to that contact; every send records the listings on the property share ledger, saves them to the contact's Portfolio shortlist as source 'shared' when they have an account (a buyer without one receives the same rows on first login), and the personal or business free-text message ends with a Portfolio nudge that names whether the buyer already has an account.

Removing an interested property is idempotent on web and mobile: the junction row and matching headline pointer are cleared together, an already-removed relationship is treated as success, and stale mobile cards disappear immediately.

Importing a phonebook contact on web or mobile fills the contact's first name, second name and Name Tag from the one device name with the same deterministic split: the Name Tag is the trailing role, trade, acronym or locality qualifier, the first name is the first given-name token plus any title or initial before it, and every remaining token is the second name. The split is a suggestion the agent can edit before or after saving, and it never sets salutation.

A contact's primary phone is the number every WhatsApp path addresses. When a contact has more than one number and none has been confirmed, the WhatsApp action on web and mobile asks once which number to message; the answer becomes the primary and is recorded on the contact so the question is never repeated. Any other number can also be made the primary from web or mobile; the swap keeps the old primary as an other number in the promoted number's slot, so no number is lost.

The Contacts area filter on web and mobile lists every locality stored on the account's contacts once per spelling group, read from GET /api/contacts/area-options which reads both area columns through account-scoped SQL functions, merges spellings of one locality under a shared key, and counts each contact once per group. Up to the same bounded number of groups can be selected at once on either surface; the list then shows a contact whose agent-entered or AI-extracted areas contain any spelling of any selected group, and the selection counts as one active filter.

A locality typed into the Contacts search box on web or mobile, or into the Requirements page search on web, whether alone or after "in", "at", "near" or "around", stands for every stored spelling of that locality: the search keys the typed text the same way the area filter keys stored areas and matches a contact whose agent-entered or AI-extracted areas contain any spelling in that group, on top of the plain text matches it already made. A term that keys to no stored locality changes nothing.
The calendar keeps the selected-day agenda visible and also makes every future scheduled appointment and every future dated open task discoverable.
Upcoming appointments and tasks are chronological and are not repeated in the selected-day agenda or the general to-do list.
Repeating or correcting the same scheduling instruction updates one appointment and produces one confirmation; it never creates a duplicate event.
A named person resolves only to the strongest unique contact match. Ambiguous names remain unlinked instead of being guessed.
Every explicitly named external attendee, including the property owner, is retained in the appointment audience so each eligible person receives timely reminders.
Correcting an appointment name, contact, property, or other non-time detail preserves its scheduled timestamp and reminder state.
Time corrections accept compact meridiem forms such as 430pm. A correction without a usable replacement date or time asks for clarification and never confirms an unchanged appointment as updated.

features.name: Brokerage invoicing and the deal document folder

invariants.rule: An invoice number is unique within its account and financial year and is never reused. A cancelled invoice keeps its number so the series has no gap, and an issued invoice never returns to draft.

An issued invoice prints the same content forever. Its issuer, customer and line items are snapshots, not joins, so editing the deal, contact or property it came from cannot change it; only a draft is editable.

Tax follows the place of supply: the same state charges CGST plus SGST in equal halves, a different state charges IGST at the full rate, and nil mode charges nothing and prints the exemption note. Known state codes override a stale stored mode, and the mode stored on the invoice is the one actually charged. Whether an invoice carries GST at all is a per-invoice toggle over the account default, so a registered brokerage can raise an exempt invoice and an unregistered one keeps its GST details ready; the exemption note is always snapshotted and printed only when that invoice charges no GST.

The billed amount is the deal value times the brokerage rate times this invoice's share, rounded to the rupee, and the same figure is shown on every surface. Totals are always recomputed server-side from the line items, never taken from the client.

A deal document is reachable only through an authenticated, account-scoped route that signs a short-lived URL. The deal-documents, generated-invoices and signatures buckets are private and no listing ever returns an object URL; the per-document route serves a redirect to the browser and the same signed link as JSON to the mobile app. Deleting a deal removes its stored objects, not only the rows that named them.

AI extraction proposes fields and never writes to an invoice by itself, and a full Aadhaar number is never stored: only the last four digits leave the file, enforced after the model returns rather than only asked for in the prompt.

An invoice file attached to a deal has exactly one home: a deal_documents row with category 'invoice' in the deal-documents bucket. There is no second store, and the folder accepts every file type the retired one did — including Word and Excel, because a brokerage's own invoice is often a workbook. Web and mobile accept the same types.

A deal document is staged straight into its own account-and-deal prefix under a server-signed, single-path upload URL rather than through the app, so the 50 MB the folder accepts is the size that actually uploads; the upload carries the file's real content type, without which storage refuses it, and a storage refusal is reported with its status and reason rather than as a retry prompt. Filing the row reads the stored object back: a path outside this account or deal, one nothing was written to, or a file that landed over the limit or of a type the folder does not take is refused and the object cleared, and the row records the size and type storage holds rather than the ones the caller declared.

Walkthrough uploads accept MP4 up to 16 MB on Starter and 100 MB on every paid plan. A failed preliminary limit lookup never makes the client deny a potentially eligible file; the upload-session endpoint authorizes the plan. Large files upload directly to Supabase with resumable chunks bound to the authorized object path, while the server verifies the completed account-scoped object before attaching it to a property.

features.name: Property inventory discovery and shortlist sharing

invariants.rule: A locality selected from Google Places finds inventory stored under the equivalent undotted abbreviation, including J. P. Nagar to JP Nagar and B.T.M. Layout to BTM Layout.
Agents can select up to 25 properties from inventory and open the existing hand-picked showcase share flow with that shortlist already selected on web and mobile.
Selecting a Google Places suggestion starts a coordinate-based nearby search on web and mobile with a 10 km locality radius, while exact multi-area matching remains a separate explicit action.
Visitors can clear every selected property at once from both the public showcase shortlist bar and its review dialog.

Search-result showcase sharing recognises text, locality, radius and inventory filters on web and mobile, resolves them to the same available published listings, and preserves per-contact Showcase Pulse attribution.

tests.case: pins the resolved results for a structured search
uses the resolved ids for a location or filtered search
pins the resolved results for a structured search

invariants.rule: When a buyer-visible property status changes, every interested or previously shared contact is told the exact new status; Under Contract is never described as Sold, while internal moderation statuses are not broadcast.

Every saved property exposes its explicit enquired contacts separately from preference-ranked matches on web and mobile, excluding view-only engagement and providing direct contact, internationally prefixed calling, personal or business WhatsApp messaging, and follow-up actions subject to the user's permissions.

When an unmapped portal ad already has a guessed property, agents can accept that mapping in one tap on web and mobile, while retaining a separate path to choose a different property; multiple ad IDs from the same portal may remain mapped to one property without replacing one another.

tests.case: [PRP-008] accepts the guessed property without reopening the picker
keeps a second ad id for the same property as an alias

invariants.rule: Every property link sent from an agent contact's Share Inventory action opens in co-broker view and carries that contact's recipient identifier, so Showcase Pulse attributes opens and listing activity to the selected contact on web and mobile.

Every property or property-selection message sent through a business WhatsApp number or handed off to a personal WhatsApp chat carries a Showcase URL attributed to the selected CRM contact; business sends repair or append the tracked URL server-side, and personal sends cannot bypass recipient selection on web or mobile.
Authenticated workspace members viewing their own public showcase never create Showcase Pulse analytics events, while signed-in members of a different workspace remain external visitors.

Sharing a listing with its matching contacts on web or mobile never asks which WhatsApp template to use: both surfaces show the engine's listing template as the server will send it (same template pick, same params), let the agent choose which of the saved listing's own photos leads the message, forward that choice to the share-property send where any photo outside the saved listing is ignored, and explain before sending why a recipient outside the 24-hour window cannot be served (no listing template submitted, awaiting Meta approval, or rejected).
Journey search finds the subject by identifying details, including normalized mobile numbers, and every active journey is classified by the most advanced stage reached by any of its items.
Closing a journey records a successful, paused or not-proceeding outcome plus a reason; archiving remains separate, and closed or archived journeys can be retrieved and reopened or restored.
Manual drag order is saved per journey mode and cannot contain duplicate subjects.

Every mirrored pipeline stage can capture an append-only, account-scoped note before or after the stage is reached; the latest note stays visible in the stage rail and the complete history retains its stage snapshot, author and creation time through closure, archival and later stage deletion.

Journey items captured automatically from WhatsApp shares stay hidden until reviewed. Both surfaces show the count and open a Captured tray where each item can be shown on the journey, all can be shown at once, or an item can be removed; showing logs an unhidden event that keeps the item's stage, and viewers can only look.

A stage card's header expands and collapses its rows, and a separate control on the header focuses the list on that stage: the other stage cards hide and the selected card is highlighted in its stage colour until the control is used again or the mode or view changes. A search runs inside the focused stage, and an empty focused stage says so and offers every stage back. On web the focused stage travels in the address so a reload keeps it. A selection whose card no longer exists shows every stage.

Inside a stage group a journey row does not repeat its stage; it shows how many of its items are still in the race with the same wording on web and mobile, greyed when there are none. Drag handles appear only when the order can actually be dragged.

Inside a stage group, an expanded journey leads with the live items resting on that stage, highlighted in the stage colour, and folds the items at other stages behind a count that opens on request; when nothing live rests on the stage, or outside a stage group, every item shows as before. Web and mobile share the split.

features.name: Saved buyer requirements and verified agent sharing

invariants.rule: A buyer requirement shared to another ConvoReal account is delivered only to the registered account resolved from a saved Agent contact, carries a structurally masked brief without buyer identity or contact details, and accepts responses only from inventory owned by the recipient account.

The account's buyer and agent requirement briefs are browsable on web and mobile from one screen: the same four counters (total, high priority, buyers, agents) each doubling as a filter, the same classification and priority filters, and one search over client, phone, brief text, notes and areas where a typed locality matches every stored spelling. Each card shows the brief the contact is actively asking about, resolving an active requirement profile when there is no primary statement, with explicit preferences winning over AI-extracted ones and the extracted ones marked as such.

A brief shared to a co-broker from either surface carries the same text: masked mode states an opaque REQ- reference and withholds the client's name, the agent's tags and notes, full mode carries them, and a parked or empty brief is never sendable. Mobile builds the message from its own copy of the digest rules, which must produce output identical to the web module for every brief and mode.

The Shared requirements search on web and mobile matches a share whose brief names a locality the typed text asks for under any spelling, alone or after "in", "at", "near" or "around", using the same spelling key as the Contacts area filter, on top of the plain text match over reference, sender, requirement text, areas, projects and property types. A term that keys to no locality changes nothing.
Primary and additional saved buyer requirements remain independently editable and deletable on web and mobile; deleting one brief never deletes the buyer contact or unrelated saved briefs.

features.name: Transaction Workspace — the closing record for a deal

invariants.rule: Converting a journey item opens exactly one deal, preserves provenance through source_journey_item_id, lands on the first active (never terminal) pipeline stage whatever the board order, seeds the default board service-side when the account has none, and leaves the journey and its history untouched; converting again returns the same deal.

deal_events is insert-only: authenticated roles hold SELECT and INSERT alone, the INSERT policy pins actor_id to the caller, and a trigger refuses UPDATE and DELETE from every role except the cascade from a deleted deal. No client edits a timeline entry.

Milestones and pipeline stages are independent: completing, skipping or reopening a milestone never changes the deal's stage or the property's status, and a stage change never completes a milestone. Both surfaces label milestone statuses identically.

Agreed consideration, registered consideration, other component, token, TDS, instrument references and brokerage received are internal-only: they are deny-listed from every external representation of a deal, never selected by /api/v1 or a public route, and never carried on a timeline event as a value.

An external audience over a bundle sees only the deals it is party to — a seller on one plot never sees the other plot's seller, terms, notes or side-only items — and a stranger sees nothing, not even an id. Every external projection passes through src/lib/deals/visibility.ts.

Token money has one source of truth per deal: a deal linked to an Owners Den room derives it from token_escrows and refuses token writes at the API and by database trigger; any other deal records token/advance directly. Both surfaces hide the token fields when Token Safe owns them.

A deal document's status only moves forward (draft → reviewed → approved → executed); approved and executed documents are superseded by a newer upload and kept, never deleted; a superseded document cannot change; all three rules hold at the API and by database trigger; expiry is a date the workspace surfaces. Both surfaces label statuses identically.

Every Transaction Workspace mutation (conversion, events, milestones, financials, documents, bundles, deal tasks) refuses read-only members through requireWriteRole, while reads remain available to viewers.

A stakeholder is a name, a role and a side on one deal and never a login. A share link is minted per stakeholder for the buyer or seller side only, its token is stored as a SHA-256 hash and shown exactly once, it expires within 30 days, it can be revoked, and every open and document fetch is logged with a hashed address. Both surfaces name the same roles, sides and expiry choices.

Every external representation of a deal — the portal view, a bundle sibling, a document fetch — is built by src/lib/deals/external-view.ts through the visibility resolver; a public deal-share route never selects a financial column, never builds its own payload, and re-checks document visibility at the byte boundary. Progress counts the whole checklist so a partial view is never presented as complete.

A sensitive link demands a per-token one-time code: six digits, hashed with the server key and bound to the link, at most five attempts, expiring in ten minutes; a successful check yields a signed unlock for that one link that expires in thirty minutes. No Supabase Auth user, session or cookie is ever created for a stakeholder, and the link itself is handed over by the agent through the share sheet or wa.me, never sent by the app.

Every timeline entry, milestone and document carries a visibility that defaults to internal; an event's visibility is fixed at insert because deal_events is immutable; notes, milestones and documents offer the same four visibilities on both surfaces.

A published update is a durable snapshot: deal_updates is insert-only (SELECT/INSERT grants, published_by pinned to the caller, UPDATE and DELETE refused by trigger except the cascade from a deleted deal), its audience is never internal, it quotes only milestones and timeline entries every reader may already see, and a correction is a new update naming supersedes_update_id while the original stays. Both surfaces compose over the same routes with the same quoting rule.

Delivery is decided honestly and recorded separately: the business number sends free-form only inside the recipient's 24-hour window and the approved purchase_progress_notice template only to a buyer outside it, personal WhatsApp is a wa.me handoff the app never sends, and sent, opened and acknowledged are three timestamps on the recipient row that are never inferred from one another. Both surfaces name the same channels and stages.

Published updates reach a stakeholder only through the external view and the visibility resolver: a side sees its own and shared updates newest first, a corrected update stays visible and marked, and an acknowledgement is recorded against the recipient row addressed through the link that resolved, never against the update as a whole.

The Records view names every row by buyer and property (unit number first), demotes a requirement-style deal title to a second line without ever repeating a converted title, and lists only closing records: a deal starts its closing record (the standard milestones) the moment it enters Negotiation/Token or a later non-lost stage through PATCH or PUT /api/deals/[id], which the board, the workspace header and mobile all use to move a stage, pausing for brokerage before a capture stage exactly as the board does, on web and mobile alike.

Deals is one surface with three views of the same rows (Board, Journey, Records) on web and mobile; the old /pipelines, /journey and /automations?tab=pipelines addresses keep landing on the matching view with their query carried across, and Automations holds only flows and analytics.

Journey stages are mirrors of the account's default pipeline stages (one journey stage per pipeline stage, same name, colour and order, kind derived from the stage name by the same words in SQL and TypeScript); there is one stage editor, the pipeline's, and a pipeline stage cannot be deleted while journey items sit on or plan for its mirror; a converted deal and its journey item stay on the same stage whichever side moved, with the journey keeping the move in its history; every journey move — web, mobile and the WhatsApp closing card — runs through one move function, and onto a mirrored stage it runs the same stage-move logic as the board (brokerage capture, closing record, property status) while a deal on another pipeline keeps its own stage; and moving a journey item into a closing or won stage opens its closing record on that very stage.

features.name: Saved WhatsApp numbers — switch the live number without a PIN

invariants.rule: Every successful Official API save (settings form, guided setup, sandbox upgrade) records the number as a saved profile keyed by phone_number_id with its encrypted token and registration state; a re-save refreshes the same profile; a phone number saved by another account, live or not, cannot be claimed.

whatsapp_config stays the single live number. Activating a saved profile keeps the outgoing number saved, copies the profile's credentials and registered_at into whatsapp_config after Meta accepts the saved token, never calls /register, and refuses to touch the live row when Meta rejects the token; the live profile cannot be deleted; summaries never carry a token.

Registration state is read from Meta (platform_type CLOUD_API), never assumed: a save without a PIN, the Verify with Meta probe, and a profile switch all record registered_at as null with Meta's reason when Meta reports the number unregistered, and a declined display name is named as that reason. A number Meta exposes no platform for (test numbers) keeps its saved state.

A switch of the live Official API number (profile activation or a save that replaces the number) records the previous display number and the switch time on whatsapp_config, and the number-change window is open for exactly seven days from that time. contact_number_update is a Utility engine template in every product language with one acknowledgement button, addressing the contact, the brokerage and the previous number.

Only a contact with one-to-one WhatsApp message history from before the switch is told about the number change, at most once per new number, whether by the notify-recent-contacts action or as the precursor the dispatcher sends ahead of any routine message inside the window: the ledger row is claimed before sending, released when the send is skipped or fails, and the notice goes free-form inside the contact's 24-hour window and by the approved template outside it, never by an unapproved template. New contacts never receive the notice, and the notice itself is never preceded by another notice.

A saved number that is not live may auto-reply to inbound messages, never the live number: the switch is refused on the live profile and cleared on activation; the reply goes from the retired number itself, quotes the inbound message, names the live number with a tap-to-chat link (or renders the saved custom message's placeholders), is sent at most once per sender per 24 hours with the ledger claimed before the send and rolled back when Meta rejects it, and every inbound message to the retired number is surfaced to the account owner as a notification whether or not a reply went out.

features.name: Contact language — the language every outbound message goes out in

invariants.rule: Every outbound template send resolves its language as contacts.preferred_language first, accounts.default_language second, English last. A null contact language means unknown and inherits the account default; an explicit 'en' is a choice and overrides a non-English account default. Language is one value per contact, never per action or per channel.

The contact's language is visible on the contact record and changeable in one tap on web and mobile, without opening the edit form, through PATCH /api/contacts/[id]/language. The picker offers exactly the product languages plus a follow-the-account-default choice, the route accepts only those codes or null, and it writes one column scoped to the caller's account.

Every language of a template shares the category Meta fixed for its name: once any variant has reached Meta, a draft or submission of another language goes out under that Meta-held category (an approved variant's category first, any Meta-held variant's otherwise), never the builder's request, and the response names the requested and assigned categories whenever they differ. A name no language of which has reached Meta keeps the requested category.

A non-English engine template has exactly one door to Meta while it is behind the review gate: the review strip's Submit to Meta, shown only after sign-off; the generic per-row Submit and Resubmit are not offered on such a row. The strip disappears while Meta holds the row pending, approved or paused, so a live translation is never offered for resubmission. A translation Meta rejected returns behind the gate: it is reworded locally, signed off again, and re-submitted through the Meta edit, which the edit route refuses (409) for an unreviewed row or for wording that differs from the signed-off body and footer. English and account-authored templates keep the generic Submit, Edit and Resubmit.

A submit Meta refuses because the language already exists is not a failure: the route looks up the variant Meta holds for that name and language and adopts its id, status, category and content (header, body, footer, buttons, samples, as Meta returns them), so the local row ends as a sync would leave it and never claims Meta holds words it refused. A refused submit of any other kind records only submission_error on a row that already carries a Meta template id, never rewrites that row's status or clears its id, and writes nothing at all when the lookup itself fails. Every submit button (one-tap engine, reviewed translation and the dialog) ignores a second click while a submit is in flight.

A send picks the recipient's language, except while Marketing to that recipient is paused, when a deliverable Utility variant of the same template wins over a Marketing one in their language. Two layers enforce it: the template loader prefers an approved Utility variant (their language, then English, then any) once it reads the contact's pause, and the dispatcher — which every send path goes through — swaps a paused Marketing send onto an approved Utility variant of the same name when it fits the parameters already built, matching the body placeholder count and the header kind, refusing the send only when none fits. A Utility variant in the recipient's own language is always the best answer, an unapproved row never beats an approved one, and a name with no fitting Utility variant behaves exactly as before.

features.name: Guidance value — Karnataka government value of a property from its sale deed schedule

invariants.rule: A schedule read is one Gemini call over an uploaded PDF or photo of at most 4 MB. Staff pay guidance_value_lookup credits, burned before the read and refunded when it fails; Portfolio buyers and owners read free under a per-person daily limit. An unsupported or oversized file is refused before any charge, and re-matching an edited schedule never reads or charges.

Matching ranks imported rates by area, road and survey number against the schedule and prefers the rate column for the schedule's type and usage: a road-specific rate of the right block beats an area-wide one, a different block or stage is demoted, and a rate whose area name shares nothing with the schedule is never offered. A schedule that names a district is matched only against that district's rates, and a subdivided survey number such as 45/2 is never treated as covered by 45/1.

Value is rate converted to per sq.ft times area: land or site area for site, house, agricultural and industrial rates, built-up area for apartment rates, plus an optional building component. A missing area yields no value and names the area to enter; a built-up area is never used as land extent.

A saved guidance value belongs to one account and a property or transaction of it, and is written only by POST /api/guidance-value/saved: members have no direct insert policy. The total is recomputed on the server from the stored rate and a snapshot of that rate is kept, so a client-sent total is ignored and deleting a notification does not change saved values.

A platform admin can import notifications straight from the IGR website: the server lists the PDFs in the guidance value table (district carried down each spanned row, Bengaluru registration districts mapped to Bengaluru Urban, BDA corrigenda listed separately) and downloads the chosen ones. Only https links on karnataka.gov.in are fetched, every redirect is re-checked against that allowlist, pages and PDFs are size-capped, and a download that is not a PDF is refused.
